newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish GDP seen growing 3.2 percent in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Spanish GDP seen growing 3.2 percent in 1997.

text.p: Spanish gross domestic product could rise by 3.2 percent in 1997 and by 3.5 percent in 1998, an independent group of economists Eriste said on Monday.
"The economic data trend allows to consider the government's forecast of 3.0 percent in 1997 and 3.2 percent in 1998 and 1999 as a realistic one," it wrote in its June report.
"If anything this forecast is too cautious. According to the data now available the Spanish economy will grow 3.2 percent in 1997 and 3.5 percent in 1998."
Although Eriste believes consumer spending will rise, it said the increase would remain below the two percent.
It expects June to show a steady inflation rate at 1.5 percent, rising to 1.6 percent in July. Then it is expected to fall in the final months of the year.
Despite a sharp improvement in the latest Spanish budget deficit, according to May data there is still a shortfall of around 150 billion pesetas, Eriste added.
This difference "is lower than the one which came from the first quarter data."

"Public budget data in May showed a recovery, for the second month in a row, of income tax receipts, this time through taxes paid by firms," it said, but it added that despite that a minibudget is still likely.
